prompt:
Two people transcribed the SAME table, the Schedule of Activities of one clinical-trial protocol. The REFERENCE transcription is taken as correct. Below are the column labels each of them wrote down. You do two things: (1) pair each REFERENCE label with the CANDIDATE label that is the same column of the source table, and (2) grade how well each paired CANDIDATE label reproduces the content of its REFERENCE label.

Each label is the header of one COLUMN of the table: a visit, contact or time point. A header is written as a path through the stacked header rows, top to bottom, joined by " > ". Each step may or may not carry the name of its header row, for example "Treatment Period > Visit Number: Visit 3 > Study Day: Day 15 > Window: ± 2 days".

STEP 1 - ALIGN
For every REFERENCE label find the CANDIDATE label that is the transcription of the same column of the source table: the same physical column, at the same place in the table.
- Both lists are in table order. Order is a strong cue: use it together with the text.
- A CANDIDATE that is evidently the transcription of a given REFERENCE column is its counterpart even if a visit number, week, day or window in it is wrong or left out; the mistakes are graded in step 2. Example: if the fourth REFERENCE column is "Visit 4 > Week 6" and the fourth CANDIDATE, sitting between the same neighbours, reads "Visit 4 > Week 8", they are the same column (graded wrong), not a null. Do not shift a whole run of columns by one to make digits agree when the order says otherwise, and do not pair by position when the CANDIDATE list has clearly dropped or inserted a column.
- Use null only when the CANDIDATE list has no counterpart for that REFERENCE column (it was skipped, or merged into another). Do not use null merely because the text differs or because you would grade it wrong.
- One-to-one: a CANDIDATE label may be used at most once. Do not assume the lists have the same length: either side may have extra columns.
- Ids carry no meaning.

STEP 2 - CHECK EACH PAIR
Compare the paired CANDIDATE text with the REFERENCE text and answer two yes/no questions (true/false).
"content": do the two texts differ in ANY character? Ignore only whitespace (spaces, line breaks). Differences of form count here and only here:
- case, punctuation, separators;
- a footnote marker written as a superscript, as a plain trailing letter or digit, glued to the word or separate ("Run-in a" / "Run-inᵃ" / "Run-ina"; in "Cycle: 2 5" against "Cycle: 2⁵" the 5 is a footnote marker, not part of the cycle number);
- an abbreviation every reader expands the same way ("Wk 6" / "Week 6"; "EOT" / "End of Treatment"; "± 7 days" / "+/-7d");
- the NAME of a header row dropped or shortened while its value is kept ("Assessment Point: Visit 9 > Study Month: Month 3" / "Visit 9 > Month: 3").
"semantic": does the CANDIDATE label mean something different from the REFERENCE label, or leave out information the REFERENCE states, so that a reader would interpret the column differently or know less about it? This covers a contradiction (typically a value is different: another visit number, week, day, month or cycle; another window size or unit (days vs weeks); a changed sign ("-2" -> "2", "±" -> "+"); another period or named visit (Screening -> Baseline)) and an omission (typically a VALUE present in the REFERENCE is absent: the week or day, the visit window ("± 2 days"), the period name, the visit number or title). Differences of form are not semantic. A dropped or shortened header-row NAME whose value is kept is not semantic.
Rules:
- "semantic" true implies "content" true.
- Footnote markers (a short letter, number or symbol attached to a label that points to a footnote): a marker that is DIFFERENT from the one in the REFERENCE, or a marker on a label whose REFERENCE has none, is semantic, because it points the reader to the wrong footnote. The same marker written in another form (superscript, attached or spaced), or a marker the CANDIDATE leaves out, is "content" only.
- Extra information in the CANDIDATE that the REFERENCE does not have, and that does not contradict it, is "content" only (footnote markers excepted, see above).
- Judge only what the two texts say. Do not guess what the source table contained.

REFERENCE COLUMN LABELS (7)
R1: "Period/Phase: Screening Period a,b,c,d > Day/Week: Day -51 to Day -1 > Window: 21 days maximum for a hospitalization admission plus up to 30 days after discharge"
R2: "Period/Phase: Double-Blind Treatment Phase > Baseline a > Day/Week: Day 1/ Randomization"
R3: "Period/Phase: Double-Blind Treatment Phase > Treatment Period > Day/Week: Week 4 (Day 28) > Window: -4/+2 days"
R4: "Period/Phase: Double-Blind Treatment Phase > Treatment Period > Day/Week: Week 12 (Day 84) > Window: -/+4 days"
R5: "Period/Phase: Double-Blind Treatment Phase > Treatment Period > Day/Week: q12wk e,f (q84d) > Window: -/+6 days"
R6: "Period/Phase: Double-Blind Treatment Phase > Treatment Period > Day/Week: Early Permanent Study Drug Discontinuation"
R7: "Period/Phase: Follow-Up After GTED > Day/Week: End of Study g > Window: 30±15 days"

CANDIDATE COLUMN LABELS (7)
C1: "Period/Phase: Screening Period a,b,c,d > Day/Week: Day -51 to Day -1 > Window: 21 days maximum for a hospitalization admission plus up to 30 days after discharge"
C2: "Period/Phase: Double-Blind Treatment Phase > Baseline a > Day/Week: Day 1/ Randomization"
C3: "Period/Phase: Double-Blind Treatment Phase > Treatment Period > Day/Week: Week 4 (Day 28) > Window: -4/+2 days"
C4: "Period/Phase: Double-Blind Treatment Phase > Treatment Period > Day/Week: Week 12 (Day 84) > Window: -/+4 days"
C5: "Period/Phase: Double-Blind Treatment Phase > Treatment Period > Day/Week: q12wke,f (q84d) > Window: -/+6 days"
C6: "Period/Phase: Double-Blind Treatment Phase > Early Permanent Study Drug Discontinuation"
C7: "Period/Phase: Follow-Up After GTED > End of Study g > Window: 30±15 days"

OUTPUT
Return only a JSON object, with no prose and no code fence, with one entry for every REFERENCE id (R1 to R7), of exactly this shape:
{"alignment": {"R1": {"c": "C1", "content": false, "semantic": false}, "R2": {"c": "C2", "content": true, "semantic": true, "reason": "week 8 instead of week 6"}, "R3": {"c": "C4", "content": true, "semantic": true, "reason": "visit window omitted"}, "R4": {"c": "C5", "content": true, "semantic": false}, "R5": null}}
"c" is a CANDIDATE id from the list above. Give both booleans for every pair. Give "reason" (at most 12 words) only when "semantic" is true; omit it otherwise. A REFERENCE with no counterpart is null.
